decisions.decision: Is the schedule set on the report itself, or in a separate step?
options: On the report — schedule fields sit inline in the report editor alongside coverage, format and recipients
A separate step — the editor saves the report definition, and scheduling is a distinct screen or stage afterwards
decisions.recommended: On the report — schedule fields sit inline in the report editor alongside coverage, format and recipients
decisions.answer: On the report — schedule fields sit inline in the report editor alongside coverage, format and recipients
decisions.rationale: Chose the recommended option at the gate 1 popup.

decisions.decision: Is a schedule a property of one report, or a reusable object several reports can share?
options: A property of one report — each report owns its own schedule
A reusable object — a named schedule several reports attach to
decisions.recommended: A property of one report — each report owns its own schedule
decisions.answer: A property of one report — each report owns its own schedule
decisions.rationale: Chose the recommended option at the gate 1 popup.

options: A stated set: daily, weekly, monthly
A stated set plus quarterly and yearly
A free recurrence builder (every N days/weeks/months, with weekday selection)
decisions.recommended: A stated set: daily, weekly, monthly
decisions.answer: A stated set: daily, weekly, monthly
decisions.rationale: Chose the recommended option at the gate 1 popup.

decisions.decision: Does run history sit on each report, or in one place for all of them?
options: On each report — history is a view within the report
One central place — a module-level history across all reports, filterable by report
Both — a central list plus a per-report view
decisions.recommended: On each report — history is a view within the report
decisions.answer: On each report — history is a view within the report
decisions.rationale: Chose the recommended option at the gate 1 popup.

decisions.decision: Does the entry point from a dashboard open the full setup page, or a short form?
options: A short form — a compact overlay capturing the minimum, with the source pre-chosen
The full setup page — navigate to the report editor with the source pre-chosen
decisions.recommended: A short form — a compact overlay capturing the minimum, with the source pre-chosen
decisions.answer: A short form — a compact overlay capturing the minimum, with the source pre-chosen
decisions.rationale: Chose the recommended option at the gate 1 popup.

decisions.decision: What does the recipient list look like at twenty addresses?
options: A chip/token field — addresses as removable tokens that wrap, with a scroll cap
A managed list — one row per address in a scrollable list with per-row remove and an add field
A textarea of addresses parsed on save
decisions.recommended: A managed list — one row per address in a scrollable list with per-row remove and an add field
decisions.answer: A managed list — one row per address in a scrollable list with per-row remove and an add field
decisions.rationale: Chose the recommended option at the gate 1 popup.

decisions.decision: May a report be emailed to an address outside the client's own organization?
options: Yes, gated on the send-outside-the-organization privilege, held by Owner and Admin only
Yes, gated on that privilege, held by Owner, Admin and Engineer
No — recipients must be inside the client's domain in this release
decisions.recommended: Yes, gated on the send-outside-the-organization privilege, held by Owner and Admin only
decisions.answer: Yes, gated on the send-outside-the-organization privilege, held by Owner and Admin only
decisions.rationale: Chose the recommended option at the gate 1 popup.

decisions.decision: Does a Technician get reports at all? Three cells of the privilege table are deliberately unfilled — see system reports, create a private report, and read run history.
options: No to all three — a Technician has no reporting surface at all
Read-only — see system reports and read run history, but cannot create
Yes to all three — a Technician may see system reports, create a private report, and read history for reports they can see
decisions.recommended: Read-only — see system reports and read run history, but cannot create
decisions.answer: Read-only — see system reports and read run history, but cannot create
decisions.rationale: Chose the recommended option at the gate 1 popup.

decisions.decision: Who designs the Dashboard Deletion Impact Dialog, given that it modifies a flow the dashboard builders own?
options: This module specs it and hands it to the dashboard builders' file
The dashboard builders own it, and this module supplies only the dependent-report data contract
This module designs and builds it in its own file, accepting a duplicate deletion flow
decisions.recommended: This module specs it and hands it to the dashboard builders' file
decisions.answer: This module specs it and hands it to the dashboard builders' file
decisions.rationale: Chose the recommended option at the gate 1 popup. Requirement 21 is this module’s requirement, but the deletion flow is not this module’s to own; needs a coordination point and a shared component location.
